lem-author-2501feae0519-finite-uniform-s.title: P. Erdős and A. Hajnal, On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems, Acta Mathematica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 17 (1966), 61–99
lem-author-2501feae0519-finite-uniform-s.locator: §13, Definition 13.2, printed p.94 (PDF p.34), and Theorem 13.3, printed p.95 (PDF p.35)
lem-author-2501feae0519-finite-uniform-s.statement: For each integer r≥3 and positive integer s there are ε>0 and n₀ such that for every integer n>n₀ there is an r-uniform set-system on n vertices which is s-circuitless and has no independent subset of more than n^(1−ε) vertices. Here s-circuitless means that every t-edge subfamily, 1≤t≤s, has union of size at least 1+(r−1)t.
lem-author-2501feae0519-finite-uniform-s.hypotheses: Fixed integers r≥3 and s≥1; n is a sufficiently large finite integer. Edges are distinct r-element subsets; independent means containing no whole edge.
lem-author-2501feae0519-finite-uniform-s.reading_limits: For this repair, read the cached full-text PDF introduction on PDF p.1 and Definition 13.2 and Theorem 13.3 on printed pp.94–95 (PDF pp.34–35); visually checked both printed pages, including the inequalities. The theorem is imported as stated, not proved locally. Only the beginning of its published proof on p.95 was read in this repair; no audit of the complete proof or reading of the whole paper is claimed. The finite r=2 case and Corollary 13.4 are not used here.
